outcome: Interval between start of ripening and delivery
cohort: Women with one previous cesarean delivery, a liveborn singleton fetus in cephalic presentation, and intact membranes, for whom cervical ripening, with unfavorable cervix (Bishop score < 6) was indicated for medical reasons.
finding: There was no significant difference between cervical ripening by double-balloon catheter and cervical ripening by prostaglandins for cesarean delivery rates, interval between start of ripening and delivery, or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in cesarean delivery rates between women who underwent cervical ripening with prostaglandins and those who underwent cervical ripening with a double-balloon catheter.
